newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: Australian Semis - Spreads mixed as yields shrink.
newsitem.headline: Australian Semis - Spreads mixed as yields shrink.

text.p: *Semi-government bond yield spreads to Australian Treasury bonds have shown a fairly mixed picture since the Easter break, although yields have shrunk in the past few days.
Semi-government bond yield spreads to Australian Treasury bonds have shown a fairly mixed picture since the Easter break, although yields have shrunk in the past few days, traders said.
A technically inspired rally in Australian bond futures has helped to bolster the physical debt market, although this has proved a signal to offer stock back on to the market.
"There are still people sitting on stock after the TCorp 2008 bond issue and semis have been notably offered both on Friday and Monday," said one trader at a European based bank.

New South Wales Treasury Corp (TCorp) introduced a new benchmark 2008 bond by tender last month, and it has also been reasonably active in the offshore markets since then, issuing issuing a A$100 million Eurobond on March 19 followed by a 35 billion yen dual currency bond on March 27.

The New South Wales state and TCorp were kept in the spolight late last month by Standard & Poor's Corp, affirming its the long term AAA and short-term A-1 plus local currency ratings and its AA/A1 plus foreign currency ratings.

S&P said this reflected the state's modest level overall indebtedness, its satisfactory ongoing financial position and the government's commitment to a disciplined medium-term fiscal framework, as well as its diversified economic base.

The affirmation follows a run of recent positive comments on the states by both S&P and Moody's Investors service, which has helped to maintain reasonably tight differentials to the Australian Treasury bonds, traders said.

Meanwhile, Queensland Treasury Corp was seen as the most likely tenderer of stock on to the semis market, having last offered on March 6, and as it usually came to the market in a four to six-week cycle, traders added.
